references.text: Pharaoh sinned again and hardened his heart, despite his confession of sin.
Pharaoh confesses his sin against the Lord and against Moses again, in a similar pattern of temporary repentance.
Balaam confesses his sin in a manner similar to what Pharaoh did.
Joshua reminds the people of the Lord's righteous acts and His power over Egypt.
The people of Israel confess their sin against the Lord in a similar way.
Saul confesses that he has sinned, similar to Pharaoh's confession.
Nehemiah refers to God's righteousness and the people's wickedness, the same contrast expressed by Pharaoh.
David acknowledges God's righteousness and his own sinfulness.
The Lord is righteous - the same description of God used by Pharaoh.
The prophet declares that the Lord is righteous, but the people have been rebellious.
Daniel confesses that righteousness belongs to the Lord, but shame belongs to the people.
The Lord is righteous in all He does - the same acknowledgment of God's righteousness.
The angel declares that the Lord is righteous in His judgments, which recalls Pharaoh's acknowledgment.
Both verses document Pharaoh's repeated admissions of sin and acknowledgment of the Lord's righteousness during the plagues.
Highlights Pharaoh's instability: an honest admission (9:27) followed by a compromise without genuine repentance (10:8).
